title: The mass density of an integer multiplicity current equals its multiplicity almost everywhere
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (an IMRep with R.Represents T), with weight μ_T = R.measure = θH^n⌞M. Then HasMassDensity T x θ(x) holds for μ_T-a.e. x. That is, θ(x) ≥ 0 and M_{B_ρ(x)}(T)/(ω_nρ^n) → θ(x) in [0, ∞] as ρ ↓ 0, where B_ρ(x) is the open ball and ω_n is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^n.
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, HasMassDensity T x (R.mult x)
